mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces consumer and business spending, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of periods following a federal funds rate increase, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in housing starts indicates increased consumer confidence and demand for new homes, which should positively impact the S&P 500 over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If housing starts rise but the S&P 500 does not show positive 60-day returns in at least 55% of cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate suggests labor market weakness, which could lead to decreased consumer spending and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the unemployment rate increases but the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 35% of cases, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production indicates stronger economic activity, which should lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If industrial production rises but the S&P 500 does not show positive 60-day returns in at least 60% of cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: If GDP growth slows while inflation increases, it indicates stagflation, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth rate decreases and CPIAUCSL increases
failure_condition: If GDPC1 growth slows and CPIAUCSL rises but the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 30% of cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 5%, it indicates a restrictive monetary policy, which could lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the federal funds rate exceeds 5% but the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of cases, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in retail sales suggests strong consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If retail sales increase but the S&P 500 does not show positive 5-day returns in at least 50% of cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: If the unemployment rate rises while payroll employment also increases, it indicates labor market contradictions, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE rises and PAYEMS increases but the S&P 500 shows positive 60-day returns in more than 35% of cases, the hypothesis is rejected.
